_comment: A synthetic run in which every ground-truth bug in libexpat-R_2_4_3.json is correctly reported. This is the fixture that proves the grader still detects its target: if the mechanism keyword lists in the ground truth stop matching a correct description, recall here drops below 7/7 and the test fails. Finding bodies are paraphrases of the real defects, not copies of any run's output.

findings.title: Integer overflow in copyString allocation size
findings.description: copyString walks the input to compute a character count and then multiplies by sizeof(XML_Char) to size the malloc. A sufficiently long string makes that product wrap, so the allocation is far smaller than the copy that follows.
findings.data_flow: source: encodingName supplied by the embedding application; sink: malloc size in copyString; validation: none
findings.impact: Heap buffer overflow when the wrapped allocation is filled at full length.
findings.recommendation: Reject lengths above SIZE_MAX / sizeof(XML_Char) before allocating.

findings.title: bufSize integer overflow in storeRawNames leads to a heap write
findings.description: bufSize is computed as nameLen + ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char)) in int arithmetic. A large rawNameLength wraps the sum, the reallocation is undersized, and the subsequent copies write past it.
findings.code:
bufSize = nameLen + ROUND_UP(tag->rawNameLength, sizeof(XML_Char));
if (bufSize > tag->bufEnd - tag->buf) { ... }
findings.data_flow: source: element name bytes in the document; sink: buffer sizing in storeRawNames; validation: none
findings.impact: Heap buffer overflow with attacker-controlled contents.
findings.mitigations_checked: no guard on the addition at expat/lib/xmlparse.c:2576
findings.recommendation: Perform the addition in a wider type and reject overflow.

findings.title: Signed overflow of neededSize past INT_MAX in XML_GetBuffer
findings.description: After the neededSize < 0 check, keep is added to neededSize with no test that keep <= INT_MAX - neededSize, so the signed int can overflow and the buffer sizing logic proceeds on a negative or tiny value.
findings.data_flow: source: len argument driven by document size; sink: neededSize arithmetic; validation: only the pre-addition negative check
findings.impact: Undersized buffer allocation followed by an out-of-bounds write.
findings.mitigations_checked: the INT_MAX guard is absent at expat/lib/xmlparse.c:2069
findings.recommendation: Check keep > INT_MAX - neededSize before the addition.
findings.fp_rationale: expat/lib/xmlparse.c:2069 adds without the INT_MAX guard

findings.title: Unsigned overflow of dtd->contentStringLen while parsing the prolog
findings.description: doProlog accumulates entity content length into contentStringLen, an unsigned int, without bounding the total, so a long enough entity wraps the counter and the size used downstream no longer describes the data.
findings.data_flow: source: entity declarations in the document prolog; sink: contentStringLen accumulation; validation: none
findings.impact: Length confusion in entity handling, leading to memory corruption.
findings.mitigations_checked: no cap on the accumulation at expat/lib/xmlparse.c:5390
findings.recommendation: Bound the accumulated length and fail on overflow.

findings.title: Unbounded recursion in build_node exhausts the stack
findings.description: build_node recurses once per child of the element content model with no depth limit, so a deeply nested model in the DTD drives recursion until the stack is exhausted.
findings.code:
for (i = 0; i < src->numchildren; i++)
  build_node(parser, src->children + i, *dest, ...);
findings.data_flow: source: element declaration nesting in the document; sink: recursive call in build_node; validation: none
findings.impact: Remote denial of service by stack exhaustion.
findings.mitigations_checked: no depth counter or limit anywhere in build_node
findings.recommendation: Convert to an explicit worklist or impose a nesting depth limit.

findings.title: Name character macros accept malformed UTF-8 because IS_INVALID_CHAR is not applied
findings.description: The name and name-start character-class macros classify a multi-byte sequence by its lead byte without first rejecting invalid encodings, so malformed UTF-8 — including an encoding of the namespace separator — is accepted as part of a name.
findings.data_flow: source: raw document bytes; sink: name-character classification; validation: IS_INVALID_CHAR is not consulted here
findings.impact: Malformed input is accepted and re-emitted, which downstream consumers parse differently.
findings.mitigations_checked: IS_INVALID_CHAR is defined but not used by these macros
findings.recommendation: Apply IS_INVALID_CHAR in the name and name-start classification paths.
findings.fp_rationale: expat/lib/xmltok_impl.c:71 omits the encoding validity check

findings.title: Namespace separator can be injected through a namespace URI in addBinding
findings.description: addBinding stores the namespace URI without rejecting the namespace separator character, so a URI containing that delimiter changes how the expanded name is later split into namespace and local part.
findings.data_flow: source: xmlns attribute value in the document; sink: binding uri stored for name expansion; validation: the separator is not rejected
findings.impact: An attacker controls how a qualified name is split, so a name can be made to appear to be in a different namespace.
findings.recommendation: Reject a URI containing the configured namespace separator.
findings.fp_rationale: expat/lib/xmlparse.c:3756 accepts the delimiter inside the value
